ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a vertical segment DB, with point C between D and B. The tick marks on DC and CB indicate DC = CB. A horizontal line passing through C reaches point A, and the right-angle mark at C indicates that AC is perpendicular to DB. Segment AD is labeled 2.5 cm, and segment AB is the unknown quantity. Reasoning: Since C is the midpoint of DB and AC is perpendicular to DB, AC is the perpendicular bisector of DB. Point A lies on this perpendicular bisector, so according to the perpendicular bisector theorem, the distances from A to D and B are equal. Therefore AD = AB. Since AD = 2.5 cm, AB = 2.5 cm.

Thus AC is the perpendicular bisector of DB. Since point A lies on this perpendicular bisector, apply the Perpendicular Bisector Theorem to conclude A is equidistant from D and B, so AD = AB. The diagram labels AD as 2.5 cm, hence AB = 2.5.
